title: The coffee queue
prompt:
Ivy, Jon, Kat, Leo and Max stand in a single-file queue. Position 1 is the front and position 5 is the back. "Directly behind" someone means the very next position toward the back.

- Jon is somewhere ahead of Leo.
- Kat is directly behind Jon.
- Ivy is directly ahead of Max.
- Max is not at either end of the queue.
- Ivy is not at the front.

How many people are standing between Kat and Leo?
hints: The queue has two side-by-side pairs and one single person. How many ways can they be arranged?
Which arrangements put Max at an end, put Ivy at the front, or put Leo ahead of Jon?
Once only one order survives, where are Kat and Leo, and who stands between them?
solution:
**2 people** (Ivy and Max).

Jon and Kat form a pair (Jon, then Kat). Ivy and Max form a pair (Ivy, then Max). Leo stands alone. Leo must be behind Jon, so he can't come before the Jon-Kat pair. That leaves three possible orders:

- Jon, Kat, Ivy, Max, Leo: Max is fourth and Ivy is third. Every clue holds.
- Ivy, Max, Jon, Kat, Leo: Ivy is at the front. Ruled out.
- Jon, Kat, Leo, Ivy, Max: Max is at the back. Ruled out.

The queue is Jon, Kat, Ivy, Max, Leo. Kat is second and Leo is fifth, so Ivy and Max stand between them.
solver:
function solve() { const names = ['Ivy','Jon','Kat','Leo','Max']; const perms = []; const build = (a, r) => { if (!r.length) { perms.push(a); return; } r.forEach((x, i) => build([...a, x], r.filter((_, j) => j !== i))); }; build([], names); const ok = perms.filter(q => { const p = x => q.indexOf(x); return p('Jon') < p('Leo') && p('Kat') === p('Jon') + 1 && p('Max') === p('Ivy') + 1 && p('Max') !== 0 && p('Max') !== 4 && p('Ivy') !== 0; }); const q = ok[0]; return Math.abs(q.indexOf('Kat') - q.indexOf('Leo')) - 1; }
return solve();
